question: Should OpenClaw accept `{ owner }` records as a persisted read shape for the existing `plugins.slots.memory` and `plugins.slots.contextEngine` config fields now, or pause this until the broader memory-slot architecture is decided?
rationale: This is a compatibility-sensitive config/API direction: automation can identify incomplete readers and proof gaps, but it cannot decide whether the persisted slot contract should expand ahead of the broader slot architecture.

options.title: Sponsor the owner-record read contract after repair
options.body: Accept the direction only if this PR or a fresh replacement fixes the blockers, proves upgrade/read behavior at the exact head, and keeps write-side canonicalization out of scope.

options.title: Pause behind broader slot architecture
options.body: Keep the idea tied to the memory role-slot discussion so the config shape is decided once with the larger slot taxonomy.

options.title: Reject this config expansion for now
options.body: Keep string-only slots until a concrete shipped plugin/API need requires provenance metadata in core config.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the owner-record read contract after repair
recommendation.body: Accept the direction only if this PR or a fresh replacement fixes the blockers, proves upgrade/read behavior at the exact head, and keeps write-side canonicalization out of scope.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans config compatibility, plugin trust, and provider-auth surfaces where recent history points to steipete as a central current-main contributor.
